agent: numeric and comparison triggers, wave 12 agent A
question: The numeric and comparison triggers: what each one reads, what it compares against, and in what units.

addresses.name: CValueTrigger::LoadArgument
addresses.comment:
**Slot 7 for the forty `CValueTrigger` leaves, and the whole reason their operands are in thousandths.** 0x5D13E0 to the single `ret 0x104` at 0x5D13FD, 8 instructions, read end to end:

    TokenToFixedPoint(&value, &local);   this->value (+0x40) = local

So the number a mod writes is multiplied by 1000 and the digits after the point are padded to exactly three - `dissent = 2` becomes 2000, `war_exhaustion = 7.5` becomes 7500 - which is the same scale the savegame prints for these keys (`neutrality=88.800`, `manpower=271.460`, `national_unity=81.752`). The leaf's `Evaluate` then either compares that straight against a thousandths field or divides it by 1000 first; see reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md for which does which.

`this` is in ECX and the 0x104-byte `CToken` arrives **by value**, which is what the `ret 0x104` cleans - the identical shape the record already gives the effect-side twin `CEffect::TakeScalarValue` (0x15FF0), whose name this borrows. **Trap 2: it abuts `CIntTrigger::LoadArgument` at 0x5D1400 with no padding at all**, so `functionStart(0x5D1400)` answers 0x5D13E0; the vftables settle both. Thirteen int3 before 0x5D13E0.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry: `lea eax,[ebp-4]; push eax; lea ecx,[ebp+8]; push ecx; call 0xA69550; mov eax,[eax]; mov [esi+0x40],eax; ret 0x104`. 0xA69550 is rva 0x669550, which project.json already records as `TokenToFixedPoint` with the thousandths semantics spelled out - so this is an independent agreement, not a new claim about the helper. `vtable.py --holding 0x9D13E0` gives 40 tables, all slot 7, and every holder derives from CValueTrigger. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a CValueTrigger leaf whose own Evaluate reads +0x40 as something other than a thousandths threshold, or a 41st holder outside the CValueTrigger family.

addresses.name: CIntTrigger::LoadArgument
addresses.comment:
**Slot 7 for the thirty-seven `CIntTrigger` leaves: `atoi`, with no scaling at all.** 0x5D1400 to three `ret 0x104` at 0x5D141D, 0x5D1434 and 0x5D1448 (one function - two `jne` jump past the first two exits), 27 instructions, read end to end:

    if (value.type == 0x377)   this->arg_is_this (+0x18) = 1; this->value (+0x40) = 0
    elif (value.type == 0x34F) this->arg_is_from (+0x19) = 1; this->value (+0x40) = 0
    else                       this->value (+0x40) = atoi(value.text)

So an int trigger's operand is the plain number, **not** thousandths, and it cannot carry decimals: `revolt_risk = 5.5` is read as 5. The two tokens are the scope keywords `this` (0x377) and `from` (0x34F) that `CEventScope::MakeScope` already handles under those names.

**Only 3 of the 37 leaves read the two flags back** (`CNumOfCitiesTrigger`, `CSubUnitTrigger`, `CUnitsInProvinceTrigger`), so for the other 34 the `keyword = this` form parses, sets the flag, zeroes the value and is then compared as `field >= 0`. **Trap 2: no padding above it** - `CValueTrigger::LoadArgument` ends `ret 0x104` at 0x5D13FD and this prologue is the next byte.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; the two immediates are `cmp eax,0x377` at 0x5D1409 and `cmp eax,0x34F` at 0x5D1420, and the atoi call is 0xB969F1, already recorded as `atoi`. `vtable.py --holding 0x9D1400` gives 37 tables, all slot 7, all CIntTrigger descendants. The flag readers come from a scan of all 168 slot-6 bodies for `this`-relative reads of +0x18/+0x19, with `CThreatTrigger` (read by hand) as the positive control. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a CIntTrigger leaf that multiplies +0x40 by 1000 and is *not* in the five-case list in the write-up, which would mean the base scale is not what this says.

addresses.name: CStringTrigger::LoadArgument
addresses.comment:
Slot 7 where the operand is a name rather than a number: `strlen(value.text)`, then `std::string::assign(this + 0x40, value.text, length)`. 0x5D1450 to the single `ret 0x104` at 0x5D1478, 19 instructions, five int3 on each side. That is the `Hoi3CString` at +0x40 the record already describes for `CCombatModifierTrigger`.

Ten holders, and only six of them are `CStringTrigger` leaves: `CHasCountryFlagTrigger`, `CHasGlobalFlagTrigger`, `CHasProvinceFlagTrigger` and `CLastMissionTrigger` derive from `CTrigger` directly and the linker folded their identical bodies into this one. The name is for the base that declares the behaviour, not a claim that those four derive from it.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; the assign is 0x40A160, which project.json records as `assign(const char*, length)` with 14075 sites. `vtable.py --holding 0x9D1450` lists the ten holders. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: an eleventh holder from an unrelated family, which would make even a base-class name misleading.

addresses.name: CBoolTrigger::LoadArgument
addresses.comment:
Slot 7 for the twenty-six `CBoolTrigger` leaves, and the whole body: `this->value (+0x40, a byte) = (value.type == 0x1F6)`. 0x5D1480 to the single `ret 0x104` at 0x5D1491, 7 instructions, five int3 before and twelve after.

Token 0x1F6 is `yes`: **anything that is not literally `yes` stores 0**, so `war = no`, `war = NO` and `war = 1` are all false, and a bool trigger can never be a parse error on its value.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry: `cmp dword ptr [ebp+8], 0x1F6; sete al; mov byte ptr [ecx+0x40], al; ret 0x104`. 0x1F6 is read as `yes` from the record's own note on `MakeFixedToken`, which builds a CToken 'whose text is `%s` of the literal `yes`'; the token table itself needs a running game. `vtable.py --holding 0x9D1480` gives 26 tables, all slot 7, all CBoolTrigger leaves. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: save token 0x1F6 turning out not to be `yes` - run `scripts/saveTokens.py` against a live game to settle it; everything else here is read off the bytes.

addresses.name: CAlwaysTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**The simplest body in the family and the whole of `always = yes`**: `mov al, byte ptr [ecx+0x40]; ret 4`. Two instructions, 0x5D3920..0x5D3925, six int3 before and ten after. It never touches the scope.

The byte at +0x40 is whatever `CBoolTrigger::LoadArgument` (0x5D1480) put there, i.e. 1 only for the literal `yes` - so `always = no` is a trigger that is always false, not a syntax error, and `always = 1` is false too.

**`image.functionStart(0x5D3920)` answers 0x5D38C0** even though the padding is clean, because the entry's first byte is `0x8A` (`mov al, byte ptr [reg+disp8]`) and that is not in the walk's prologue set - the second cause under trap 2, and a new byte for that list.
addresses.evidence: Six bytes read with `disasm.py --bytes` (`8a 41 40 c2 04 00`); the function above ends `ret 0x10` at 0x5D3917 and 0x5D391A..0x5D391F are int3. `vtable.py --holding 0x9D3920` gives exactly one table, CAlwaysTrigger slot 6, and slot 8 is 0x5D3930, which bounds it from above. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: +0x40 having a writer other than slot 7 - there is none in this body and the base constructor at 0x5CDC30-style zeroes it.

addresses.name: CDissentTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**The canonical seventeen-instruction `CValueTrigger` body, read end to end**, and the shape thirteen of the forty leaves share:

    country = g_CCountryDataBase[0x1A855A4]->+0x16C[ scope->country_id (+0x14) ]
    return country->dissent (+0x10B4) >= this->value (+0x40)      ; setge, signed

0x5F90F0 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5F9123, four int3 before and ten after. `scope->country_tag (+0x10)` is loaded and stored to a dead stack slot - the inlined remains of a by-value `CCountryTag` - and only the id half is used.

Units: +0x40 is thousandths (slot 7) and `dissent` is thousandths (the save writes `dissent=0.000`), so **the number a mod writes is the number the save shows**: `dissent = 5` fires at 5.000. The comparison is `>=`, which its own `GetBlockText` (0x5F9130) corroborates by rendering the negated form through the localisation key `DISSENT_IS_NOT_TRIGGER`.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry. +0x10B4 is already `dissent` in project.json's CCountry record, and [0x1A855A4]+0x16C is the country database array it names in a dozen comments. The scale is checked against a save: `grep -o 'dissent=[0-9.]*'` over Ireland1945_01_22_02.hoi3 returns values with exactly three decimals. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a `dissent` key in a save with more or fewer than three decimals, or a reading of slot 7 that did not multiply by 1000.

addresses.name: CWarexhaustionTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
`country->war_exhaustion (+0xAD0) >= this->value (+0x40)`, the same seventeen instructions as `CDissentTrigger::Evaluate` with one displacement changed. 0x5D3BE0 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5D3C13, six int3 before and ten after.

Thousandths both sides, so the script number is the number the save prints - and a 1945 BlackICE save carries `war_exhaustion` up to 7570.000, so a condition written `war_exhaustion = 10` is satisfied the moment war exhaustion passes ten, not ten percent of anything. Its `GetBlockText` (0x5D3C20) renders the negated form as `WAR_EXHAUSTION_LESS_THAN`, which is independent agreement that the test is `>=`.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; +0xAD0 is `war_exhaustion` in both project.json's CCountry record and BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp, named there from the save key. The save check is `grep -o 'war_exhaustion=[0-9.]*'`, which returns 107 zeros and a spread of three-decimal values up to 7570.000. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the field being a percentage somewhere else in the image, i.e. a reader that divides it by 1000 before display.

addresses.name: CManpowerTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
`country->manpower (+0xBCC) >= this->value (+0x40)`, the canonical seventeen-instruction `CValueTrigger` body. 0x5EFC20 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5EFC53, thirteen int3 before and ten after.

**The linker folded two classes onto it: `CManpowerTrigger` and `CMaxManpowerGreaterThanTrigger`, both at slot 6.** They are siblings under `CValueTrigger`, not one derived from the other, so the fold means their source bodies are identical - and therefore `max_manpower_greater_than = N` tests **current** manpower (+0xBCC), not max manpower (+0xBD0, which is what `CMaxManpowerTrigger::Evaluate` at 0x5D4620 reads). The name here is for the class the behaviour belongs to; the slot is recorded for both.

Thousandths both sides: a save shows `manpower=271.460`, so `manpower = 271.46` is the same quantity.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; `vtable.py --holding 0x9EFC20` prints exactly two tables, CManpowerTrigger slot 6 and CMaxManpowerGreaterThanTrigger slot 6, and hoi3.classes() gives both `CValueTrigger` as their only base. The companion body at 0x5D4620 differs only in reading +0xBD0. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: `CMaxManpowerGreaterThanTrigger` having a second slot-6 body somewhere - it does not; its table points here.

addresses.name: CMaxManpowerTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
`country->max_manpower (+0xBD0) >= this->value (+0x40)`, the canonical seventeen-instruction `CValueTrigger` body. 0x5D4620 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5D4653, twelve int3 before and ten after. Thousandths both sides.

This is the only trigger that reads +0xBD0 directly; `CManpowerPercentTrigger::Evaluate` uses it as the denominator, which is the second witness for the field's name.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: +0xBD0 turning out to be something other than the manpower ceiling, which the ratio in 0x5D4EA0 would then be nonsense.

addresses.name: CManpowerPercentTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`manpower_percentage` is a fraction, not a percentage.** 0x5D4EA0 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5D4F0A, 43 instructions, read end to end; twelve int3 before, three after.

    country = db->+0x16C[scope->country_id]
    return __alldiv(__allmul(country->manpower (+0xBCC), 1000), country->max_manpower (+0xBD0))
           >= this->value (+0x40)

Both fields are thousandths so they cancel: the left side is the ratio in per-mille, 0..1000. The right side is the script number times 1000. The condition is therefore `manpower / max_manpower >= <script number>`, so **`manpower_percentage = 0.5` means half** and `manpower_percentage = 50` can only be met if a country has fifty times its own manpower ceiling, i.e. never.

It does not guard the divide: a country with `max_manpower == 0` faults here. No such country has been observed, so this is a note about the body rather than a reachable bug.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry: `push 0; cdq; push 0x3e8; push edx; push eax; call 0xB99AF0` with eax = [country+0xBCC], then `__alldiv` (0xB99980) by [country+0xBD0], then `cmp eax, ebx; setge` with ebx = this->+0x40 loaded at 0x5D4EB0. Both helpers are already recorded as `__allmul`/`__alldiv`. The arithmetic is the whole argument: no scale assumption is needed, only that slot 7 multiplies by 1000, which is read from 0x5D13E0. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: `CValueTrigger::LoadArgument` not being this class's slot 7 - its table says it is.

addresses.name: CNationalUnityTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
`country->national_unity (+0x10B8) >= this->value (+0x40)`, the canonical seventeen-instruction `CValueTrigger` body. 0x5F33A0 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5F33D3, twelve int3 before and ten after.

Thousandths both sides, and the save prints `national_unity=81.752`, so `national_unity = 80` is eighty points of unity.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; the field is corroborated twice over - the save key, and `CCountry::GetSurrenderProgress` (0xFCB80) reading +0x10B8 and dividing it by 100 to get a 0..1000 number, which only works if +0x10B8 runs to 100000. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a save whose `national_unity` exceeds 100.000.

addresses.name: CNeutralityTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`neutrality = N` reads `effective_neutrality` (+0xA90), not `neutrality` (+0xA8C).** The canonical seventeen-instruction `CValueTrigger` body; 0x5F9430 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5F9463, thirteen int3 before and ten after. Thousandths both sides.

The raw field is what `base_neutrality` (`CBaseNeutralityTrigger::Evaluate`, 0x5F9470, the very next function) reads. project.json already describes +0xA90 as 'Neutrality minus the threat the country feels from one single country, floored at zero and capped at 100000', and the two can be far apart: a 1945 BlackICE save has Ireland at `neutrality=88.800` and `effective_neutrality=0.000`. So the two keywords are the other way round from what their names suggest, and `neutrality = 50` on a threatened country is false while `base_neutrality = 50` is true.
addresses.evidence: Both bodies decoded from their entries; the only difference is `cmp dword ptr [eax+0xa90], ecx` at 0x5F9457 against `cmp dword ptr [eax+0xa8c], ecx` at 0x5F9497. +0xA90 is already `effective_neutrality` in project.json and CLASSES.md line 1549 already says 'Neutrality is +0xA8C and EffectiveNeutrality +0xA90'. The save values are from Ireland1945_01_22_02.hoi3. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: project.json's +0xA90 reading being the mistaken one, which the save's own two separate keys rule out.

addresses.name: CBaseNeutralityTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment: `country->neutrality (+0xA8C) >= this->value (+0x40)`, the canonical seventeen-instruction `CValueTrigger` body and the twin of `CNeutralityTrigger::Evaluate` 0x40 bytes above it. 0x5F9470 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5F94A3, ten int3 before and ten after. Thousandths both sides; the save writes `neutrality=88.800`. This is the *raw* neutrality, before the highest-threat subtraction.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; see the note on 0x5F9430. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the save's `neutrality` key being written from +0xA90 instead, which the presence of a separate `effective_neutrality` key in the same block excludes.

addresses.name: CBlockadeTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment: `country->+0xBD4 >= this->value (+0x40)`, the canonical seventeen-instruction `CValueTrigger` body. 0x5D4100 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5D4133, twelve int3 before and ten after. Thousandths both sides - the field is unnamed elsewhere and this is the `blockade` keyword's only reader, so the field is reported, and named only `inferred`, under struct_fields.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; the body is byte for byte the dissent one with the displacement changed. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing about the body; the uncertainty is entirely in what +0xBD4 holds.

addresses.name: CLostICTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment: `country->+0x1158 >= this->value (+0x40)`, the canonical seventeen-instruction `CValueTrigger` body - so **`lost_IC` is on the thousandths scale**, unlike `total_ic` four entries away, which divides the operand by 1000. 0x5F86D0 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5F8703, three int3 before and ten after.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; the absence of the divide-by-1000 magic (0x10624DD3) in the body is what distinguishes the two families, and it was checked over all 168 slot-6 bodies by script. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: +0x1158 being a whole-IC field, which would make the keyword unusable as written - that is the open question recorded against the field.

(The class name's missing `r` is the game's, not a transcription slip.)

(`Stat`, not `Strat`, is the game's own class name.)

addresses.name: CTotalICTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**The second `CValueTrigger` shape: twenty-five instructions, and the eight extra ones divide the operand by 1000.** 0x5FEB50 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5FEB97, fifteen int3 before and six after.

    threshold = this->value (+0x40) / 1000               ; mov eax,0x10624DD3; imul ecx; sar edx,6; +sign
    country   = db->+0x16C[scope->country_id]
    return country->base_ic (+0x604) >= threshold

So `total_ic = 100` becomes 100000 at load and 100 again here, and is compared against **whole** IC. The mod writes plain IC, which is what BlackICE's 90-odd `total_ic = <n>` conditions assume. project.json already records +0x604 as `base_ic`, with +0x608 `lend_lease_ic` noted as being 'in whole IC' - the same scale.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry. 0x10624DD3 with `sar edx,6` is the standard signed divide-by-1000 magic (2^38/1000 = 274877906.9), and the value divided is `ecx`, loaded from `[ecx+0x40]` at 0x5FEB5F - i.e. the operand, not the field. Which side is divided was checked instruction by instruction for every scaling body in the family, because `CBuildingTrigger` divides the *field* with the same magic. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: +0x604 holding thousandths, which would make `total_ic = 100` mean 0.1 IC.

addresses.name: CTotalSeaBattlesTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment: `country->+0x1070 >= this->value (+0x40) / 1000`, the twenty-five-instruction operand-divided `CValueTrigger` shape. 0x600060 to the single `ret 4` at 0x6000A7, twelve int3 before and six after. So `total_sea_battles = 5` means five, and the field is a plain count.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; `mov ecx,[ecx+0x40]` at 0x60006F then the divide-by-1000 magic at 0x60007A, so the operand is the side scaled. The four `total_*` fields +0x1070..+0x107C sit immediately below the three already-named `*_battles_fought` counters at +0x1080/+0x1084/+0x1088. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the field being thousandths, which would make every one of these four conditions off by a thousand - it is the reason they are reported here rather than assumed.

BlackICE's two uses (`total_offensives = 5`, `= 10`) read as plain counts, which is what this says.

addresses.name: CAirBattlesFoughtTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**The canonical seventeen-instruction `CIntTrigger` body, and the family's cleanest units check.** 0x601AC0 to the single `ret 4` at 0x601AF3, four int3 before and ten after.

    country = db->+0x16C[scope->country_id]
    return country->air_battles_fought (+0x1084) >= this->value (+0x40)

No scaling anywhere: slot 7 for a `CIntTrigger` is `atoi`, the field is a plain count, and the savegame writes it as a plain integer (`air_battles_fought=7`). So the three `*_battles_fought` triggers are the one place where the script number, the field and the save all agree without a factor of 1000 - which is exactly what makes them the control for everything else here.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry. +0x1084 is already `air_battles_fought` in project.json, named from the save key, and the save writes it with no decimal point at all while `war_exhaustion` in the same block has three - two different writers for two different scales, agreeing with the two different trigger bases. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a save with `air_battles_fought=7.000`.

addresses.name: CNumOfRevoltsTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
`country->+0xF50 >= this->value (+0x40)`, the canonical seventeen-instruction `CIntTrigger` body, no scaling, so a plain count of provinces in revolt. 0x5D73D0 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5D7403, thirteen int3 before and ten after.

**This settles an open item in findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md**, whose section 8 lists `CCountry +0xF50` as an unnamed int that `CAIUnit` slot 73 tests `> 0` as an alternative to `at_war`. Two triggers read it - this one as `num_of_revolts` and `CNumOfRevoltsFractionTrigger` (0x5D7950) as the numerator of `revolt_percentage` over `NumberOfOwnedProvinces` - which gives it a count of revolting provinces, and makes the AI's test 'am I fighting rebels' rather than anything to do with war.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry, and from 0x5D7950 where +0xF50 is divided by +0xCF8 (`NumberOfOwnedProvinces`, already named) - a count over a count. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: +0xF50 being a thousandths quantity, which the division by a raw province count excludes.

addresses.name: CNumOfRevoltsFractionTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`revolt_percentage` is a fraction, not a percentage** - the same arithmetic as `manpower_percentage`. 0x5D7950 to two `ret 4` at 0x5D7A05 and 0x5D7A0C (one function: the `jl` at 0x5D79FA and the `je` at 0x5D7981 both land on the second), 70 instructions, read end to end.

    country = db->+0x16C[scope->country_id]
    if (country->NumberOfOwnedProvinces (+0xCF8) == 0) return false
    ratio = (country->+0xF50 * 1000) * 1000 / (country->+0xCF8 * 1000)      ; = revolts * 1000 / owned
    return ratio >= this->value (+0x40)

Both counts are multiplied by 1000 first - the engine's fixed-point idiom - so the left side is per-mille of the fraction and the right side is the script number times 1000. Hence `revolt_percentage = 0.3` is thirty percent and `revolt_percentage = 30` is unreachable. The 64-bit `__allmul`/`__alldiv` arm is the same overflow guard `TokenToFixedPoint` uses and computes the same value as the 32-bit arm.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry: `imul eax,eax,0x3e8` on [country+0xF50] at 0x5D79A4, `imul esi,esi,0x3e8` on [country+0xCF8] at 0x5D79B0, then either `imul eax,eax,0x3e8; cdq; idiv esi` (0x5D79CD) or `__allmul`/`__alldiv`, then `cmp eax,[edi+0x40]; jl`. The `lea edx,[eax+0x189373]; cmp edx,0x39580D` range test picking between the arms is the same pair of constants project.json already identifies in `TokenToFixedPoint`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: slot 7 for this class not being 0x5D13E0 - its table says it is.

addresses.name: CTechnologyTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**The busiest leaf in the family - 33,204 live instances - and three instructions of pointer walking.** 0x5DB430 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5DB478, 23 instructions, seven int3 before and five after.

    country = db->+0x16C[scope->country_id]
    levels  = country->technology_status (+0xDF8)->level_by_technology (+0x218)
    return levels[ this->technology (+0x44)->index (+0x244) ] >= this->value (+0x40)

So `divisonal_command_structure = 1` is 'researched level at least 1', the operand is a plain integer (`CIntTrigger`, `atoi`), and the technology itself is resolved at load time into a pointer at **+0x44** - a field past `CValueTrigger`'s single dword, so this class is larger than the 0x44 bytes `CTrigger::LoadKey` allocates for the plain ones.

**Trap 14, decisively**: `CTechnologyStatus +0x218` is already recorded as `level_by_technology`, 'ints indexed by a technology's index (`CTechnology +0x244`)'. Both halves of the index chain were already in the record under those names, which is as strong an agreement as this kind of reading gets.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; `mov eax,[eax+0xdf8]; mov eax,[eax+0x218]` then `mov edx,[ecx+0x44]; mov edx,[edx+0x244]; mov edx,[eax+edx*4]; cmp edx,[ecx+0x40]; setge`. The two field names come from project.json, not from this reading. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: +0x44 holding something other than a CTechnology* - which `CTechnology +0x244` being the array's own index makes very hard.

addresses.name: CAmountOfBrigadesTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`total_amount_of_brigades` counts every regiment of every land unit except HQ brigades.** 0x5F3E90 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5F3F78, 78 instructions with an SEH frame, read end to end.

    hq = CSubUnitDataBase::GetInstance()->hq_brigade (+0x78)->type_index (+0x24)
    country = db->+0x16C[scope->country_id]
    count = 0
    for unit in country->units (+0xBAC):                     ; CList, data at +0, next at +8
        if (unit->slot15() && unit->regiments (+0x38)):      ; slot 15 is the land predicate
            for sub in unit->regiments:
                if (sub->sub_unit_definition_ptr (+0x58)->type_index (+0x24) != hq) ++count
    return count >= this->value (+0x40)

The operand is a plain integer (`CIntTrigger`, `atoi`) and the count is a plain count, so no scale question arises. It also creates the `CSubUnitDataBase` singleton if it does not exist, inline, the same lazy accessor the record already describes at 0x1ADEA2.

**Trap 2: zero padding above it.** The preceding function ends `ret 0x10` at 0x5F3E8D and this prologue is the very next byte, so `functionStart(0x5F3E90)` answers `CAmountOfDivisionsTrigger::Evaluate` at 0x5F36E0 with two `ret`s in between. The vftable settles it: 0x5F3E90 is slot 6 of CAmountOfBrigadesTrigger and slot 8 is 0x5F3F80, five int3 later.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry. Three of the four field names are already in project.json and agree: `CSubUnitDataBase +0x78` is `hq_brigade`, `CSubUnit +0x58` is `sub_unit_definition_ptr`, `CSubUnitDefinition +0x24` is `type_index`, and 'unit slot 15, [vftable+0x3C]' is already described as the land predicate in the `land_brigades_in_service` comment. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: +0x78 being some other cached definition - the record names all 33 of them and only one is at +0x78.

addresses.name: CVariableTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`check_variable`, 12,815 live instances, and it has a side effect.** 0x5F01D0 to three `ret 4` at 0x5F022A, 0x5F024A and 0x5F0255 (one function; the two `je` at 0x5F01E5 and 0x5F0219 jump past the earlier exits), 56 instructions, read end to end.

    if (scope->country_id (+0x14) == 0) return false
    country = db->+0x16C[scope->country_id]
    found = country->variables (+0x1AC)->slot1(&this->name (+0x40))
    if (!found) { 0x76FB0(&this->name, 0);  return 0 >= this->value (+0x5C) }
    return found->+0x1C >= this->value (+0x5C)

So the class keeps the name as a `Hoi3CString` at +0x40 and the threshold at +0x5C, both written by its own `CVariableTrigger::LoadKey` (0x5F0260, already recorded, keys `which` and `value`). **The threshold goes through `TokenToFixedPoint`, so it is thousandths** - `mov [edi+0x5C], eax` at 0x5F02B4 straight off that call - which matches the savegame, where variables print with three decimals (`BaseIC=35.000`).

Two consequences for a mod: **testing a variable that does not exist creates it, set to zero**, and the test then answers `0 >= value`, so `check_variable = { which = never_set value = 0 }` is true. And the comparison is `>=`, not equality.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; the `value` parse is read from CVariableTrigger::LoadKey at 0x5F02AD (`call 0xA69550; mov eax,[eax]; mov [edi+0x5C],eax`). +0x1AC is already `variables` in project.json's CCountry record. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: 0x76FB0 turning out to be a lookup rather than an insert, which would make the side-effect claim wrong while leaving the rest standing - it is on the frontier for that reason.

addresses.name: CEnemyIcRatioTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; `setle` at 0x608165, 0x608197, 0x6081AC and 0x60813B, `imul eax,eax,0x3e8` on [country+0x60C] at 0x6080F4 and on each enemy at 0x608113, `imul eax,eax,0x3e8; cdq; idiv esi` at 0x608155. +0x60C `max_ic`, +0xACC `at_war` and +0x1008 `enemies` (with the 0x14-byte node layout, id at +4, next at +0xC) are all already named in project.json and all three fit. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the comparison being `setge` - it is `0f 9e`, not `0f 9d`, at all four sites.

addresses.name: CSurrenderProgressTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`surrender_progress` is on a 0..100 scale, so BlackICE's `surrender_progress = 0.05` conditions are satisfied by almost any progress at all.** 0x5F8210 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5F826B, 31 instructions, read end to end.

    country  = db->+0x16C[scope->country_id]
    progress = *CCountry::GetSurrenderProgress(country, &slot)        ; 0 .. 1000, clamped
    return __alldiv(__allmul(progress, 100000), 1000) >= this->value (+0x40)

The left side is `progress * 100`, i.e. 0..100000; the right side is the script number times 1000. So the condition is `progress / 10 >= <script number>` with `progress / 10` running 0..100. `surrender_progress = 80` is a meaningful threshold; `surrender_progress = 0.05` asks for `progress >= 1` out of 1000.

**Trap 2 and trap 3 together on the extent.** Only *two* int3 separate it from the next function, and a decode that walks a three-int3 run as its boundary runs 0x460 bytes past the end into a body that ends `ret 0x10`. The `ret` immediates settle it - a `ret 4` and a `ret 0x10` cannot be one `__thiscall` - and so does the vftable: slot 8 is 0x5F8270.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; `push 0x186a0` (100000) at 0x5F8247 into `__allmul`, `push 0x3e8` at 0x5F8255 into `__alldiv`, then `cmp eax,[esi+0x40]; setge`. The 0..1000 range of the left operand is read from `CCountry::GetSurrenderProgress` itself (0xFCB80), which clamps with `test eax,eax; jns` and `cmp eax,0x3e8; jle; mov eax,0x3e8`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: GetSurrenderProgress returning something outside 0..1000 on some path - all three of its exits were read and all are clamped or literal.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetSurrenderProgress
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry. The name is likely, and the reason it is only likely is that the sole evidence for it is the keyword of its single caller: `findRefs.py --callers` on 0xFCB80 finds one call site, 0x5F823D, inside the body of the `surrender_progress` trigger. The 0..1000 range is read off the clamp (`xor eax,eax` when negative at 0xFCC39, `mov eax,0x3e8` when above 1000 at 0xFCC42) and is `confirmed` in its own right. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a second caller giving the value a different meaning, or 0xFCC60 (unnamed, on the frontier) turning out to compute something unrelated to surrender.

addresses.name: CCombatTemperatureTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**Twelve instructions, and the clearest statement of the `CIntTrigger` scale rule: the operand is scaled up rather than the field down.** 0x607E50 to the single `ret 4` at 0x607E6F, four int3 before and fourteen after.

    threshold = this->value (+0x40) * 1000
    province  = scope->combatant (+0x40)->combat (+0x3C)->+0x18
    return province->+0x7C < threshold                           ; setl

So `province_temperature = N` is true when the province's temperature - a thousandths field - is **below** N, and it is one of the two numeric triggers in the family that tests `<` rather than `>=`. It is a combat-scope trigger: it reads `CEventScope +0x40`, which is the `CCombatant`, and would fault on an ordinary country scope where that field is 0.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry: `mov eax,[ecx+0x40]; mov ecx,[ebp+8]; imul eax,eax,0x3e8; mov edx,[ecx+0x40]; mov ecx,[edx+0x3c]; mov edx,[ecx+0x18]; cmp [edx+0x7c],eax; setl al`. `CCombatant +0x3C` is already `combat` in project.json. Which side the 0x3e8 multiplies is read off the instruction, not assumed. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: `[combat+0x18]` not being a province - its +0x7C would then be some other thousandths quantity, and the scale claim would stand while the name would not.

addresses.name: CBuildingTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**The one body in the family that divides the *field* by 1000 instead of scaling the operand**, which is why a scan for the divide-by-1000 magic must look at the instruction and not just at the class's base. 0x5DC040 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5DC112, 69 instructions, seven int3 before and eleven after.

    state    = g_CCurrentGameState[0x1A89790]                       ; the lazy accessor, inlined
    province = state->+0xB8C[ scope->province (+0x28) ]
    level    = province->+0x310[ this->building (+0x44)->+0x54 ]->+0x20
    return level / 1000 >= this->value (+0x40)

The operand is a plain integer (`CIntTrigger`, `atoi`) and the stored level is thousandths, so `<building_name> = 3` means level 3. Like `CTechnologyTrigger` it keeps the thing it names in a pointer at +0x44, resolved at load time.

Its keyword is **not** in `CTrigger::LoadKey`'s 152-case table (`findings/FINDINGS-script.md`'s trigger list has `has_building` for `CHasBuildingTrigger` and nothing for this class), so it is reached through the loader's default arm - which is consistent with the key being a building's own name.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; `mov eax,0x10624dd3; imul dword ptr [edx+0x20]; sar edx,6` at 0x5DC0EE - the memory operand is the field, and the operand at +0x40 is untouched until the `cmp` at 0x5DC100. The inlined `g_CCurrentGameState` accessor ([0x1A89790], 0xDA8 bytes, vftable 0x15CF674, the +0xD9C/+0xDA0/+0xDA4 clears) is the one project.json describes 2,772 copies of. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: province +0x310 not being the per-building array, which would leave the scale claim standing and the rest unnamed.

addresses.name: CThreatTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry: `mov esi,[ecx+0x48]; imul esi,esi,0x3e8` at 0x5F2C4E, `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x18],0` at 0x5F2C57, `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x19],0` at 0x5F2C6E, and `call 0x9C1A40` - rva 0x5C1A40, which wave 11 recorded as `EventScope_GetCountryTag`. The atoi into +0x48 is read in LoadKey at 0x5F2D0A/0x5F2D12. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a second writer of +0x48 that scales, which would double-scale the threshold.

addresses.name: CRulingPopularityTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
The `popularity` keyword, 37 instructions, 0x5F9EF0 to two `ret 4` at 0x5F9F46 and 0x5F9F50 (one function; the `jl` at 0x5F9F3D lands on the second), thirteen int3 after.

    country = db->+0x16C[scope->country_id]
    ruling  = country->+0x1140
    if (!ruling) return false
    return country->+0x10FC[ ruling->+0x4C ] >= this->value (+0x40)

`CValueTrigger`, no scaling in the body, so the field is thousandths and `popularity = 30` is thirty points. Only **one** int3 separates it from the function above - the vftable is what settles the entry, and 0x5F9EF0 is CRulingPopularityTrigger slot 6.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; the twin at 0x5F97B0 is the same body with +0x10C4 in place of +0x10FC, which is what makes the pair of arrays legible. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: +0x1140 not being the ruling party, which would leave the scale claim and invalidate the field names.

addresses.name: CRulingOrganisationTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
The `organisation` keyword - the ruling party's organisation, not a unit's. 0x5F97B0 to two `ret 4` at 0x5F9806 and 0x5F9810, 37 instructions, thirteen int3 either side. Instruction for instruction `CRulingPopularityTrigger::Evaluate` with `country->+0x10C4` in place of `+0x10FC`:

    ruling = country->+0x1140;  if (!ruling) return false
    return country->+0x10C4[ ruling->+0x4C ] >= this->value (+0x40)

`CValueTrigger`, no scaling in the body, so thousandths.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; see 0x5F9EF0. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: as for 0x5F9EF0.

struct_fields.name: neutrality
struct_fields.comment: **Neutrality before the highest-threat subtraction**, in thousandths - the field `base_neutrality = N` reads. `effective_neutrality` at +0xA90 is the derived one, already recorded, and it is what the plain `neutrality = N` keyword reads instead.
struct_fields.evidence: Three agreeing sources, none of them new: `CLASSES.md` line 1549 already says 'Neutrality is +0xA8C and EffectiveNeutrality +0xA90'; `BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp` line 303 says the Lua API gives +0xA8C the key `neutrality`; and the savegame writes `neutrality=88.800` and `effective_neutrality=0.000` as two separate keys in the same country block, which is what rules out their being one field. This reading adds a fourth: `CBaseNeutralityTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F9470) reads +0xA8C and `CNeutralityTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F9430) reads +0xA90. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing short of all four being wrong together.

struct_fields.name: manpower
struct_fields.comment: **The country's manpower pool, in thousandths.** The field `manpower = N` reads, and - because the linker folded the two bodies - the field `max_manpower_greater_than = N` reads as well, which is almost certainly not what that keyword's name promises.
struct_fields.evidence: Already named on the C++ side, which is trap 14's point about the fact base having two halves: `BiceLib/Hooks/Tooltips/ManpowerText.cpp` patches `add dword ptr [esi+0xBCC], eax` as 'where the manpower comes back', TRAPS.md records that the Lua API named +0xBCC `Manpower`, and project.json's own `starting_manpower` (+0x158) comment says 'LoadKey copies Manpower here'. The scale is from the savegame: `manpower=271.460` in a country block, three decimals. This reading adds `CManpowerTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5EFC20) and `CManpowerPercentTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D4EA0) as readers. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing; this entry exists to put the name in project.json, where it was missing.

struct_fields.name: max_manpower
struct_fields.comment: **The manpower ceiling, in thousandths** - the field `max_manpower = N` reads, and the denominator of `manpower_percentage`.
struct_fields.evidence: Two readers that agree: `CMaxManpowerTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D4620) compares it against the `max_manpower` keyword's operand, and `CManpowerPercentTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D4EA0) divides `manpower` (+0xBCC) by it to get a fraction. A field that is both 'what max_manpower means' and 'the denominator manpower is a fraction of' is the ceiling. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a third reader treating it as something else; two readers in the same family is thin, which is why the ratio is doing the work here rather than the keyword alone.

struct_fields.name: blockade
struct_fields.comment: Thousandths. **Likely** the blockade level the `blockade = N` keyword tests, and likely only because the single reader found is `CBlockadeTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D4100), whose class name is the whole of the evidence for the name. It sits immediately after `manpower` and `max_manpower`.
struct_fields.evidence: One reader, decoded from 0x5D4100, which is the canonical `CValueTrigger` body with +0xBD4 as its displacement; `findings/FINDINGS-script.md` gives `CBlockadeTrigger` the keyword `blockade`. The thousandths part is structural - `CValueTrigger` with no divide in the body - and is as firm as the rest of that family. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: another reader giving the field a wider meaning, exactly trap 14's `tutorial_active` case; and the savegame does not write a `blockade` key for a country, so that oracle is unavailable here.

struct_fields.name: provinces_in_revolt
struct_fields.comment:
**How many of the country's provinces are in revolt**, as a plain count. `findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md` section 8 lists this offset as an open question - 'an int slot 73 tests `> 0` as an alternative to `at_war`' - and this is the answer: the AI is asking whether it is fighting rebels.

Two triggers read it. `CNumOfRevoltsTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D73D0) is the `num_of_revolts` keyword, comparing it against a raw `CIntTrigger` operand; `CNumOfRevoltsFractionTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D7950) is `revolt_percentage`, dividing it by `NumberOfOwnedProvinces` (+0xCF8).
struct_fields.evidence: Both trigger bodies decoded from their entries. The count - rather than thousandths - follows from the division: 0x5D7950 scales both +0xF50 and +0xCF8 by 1000 before dividing, which is the engine's idiom for two integers, and +0xCF8 is already recorded as a province count. The class names come from `findings/FINDINGS-script.md`'s keyword table. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the AI's `> 0` test at 0x8B0CCC meaning something incompatible with 'provinces in revolt' - it reads as the same thing, which is the corroboration, not the claim.

struct_fields.name: num_of_ports
struct_fields.comment: A plain count. **Likely** the country's own ports, read by `CNumOfPortsTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D84D0) for the `num_of_ports` keyword. The four counters at +0x105C, +0x1060, +0x1064 and +0x1068 are read by four consecutive `CIntTrigger` leaves and form one run.
struct_fields.evidence: The body at 0x5D84D0 is the canonical seventeen-instruction `CIntTrigger` shape with +0x105C as its displacement, identified by matching its instruction count, its displacement set and its single global against `CAirBattlesFoughtTrigger::Evaluate`, which was read end to end. The keyword is from `findings/FINDINGS-script.md`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: another reader, or the savegame writing a `num_of_ports` key with decimals - it writes no such key, so the scale rests on the trigger base alone.

struct_fields.name: total_num_of_ports
struct_fields.comment: A plain count. **Likely** ports including those of subjects or faction partners - the `total_num_of_ports` keyword's field, read by `CTotalNumOfPortsTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D8A50). Which of the two counts is 'total' is not established; only that the keyword reads this one and `num_of_ports` reads +0x105C.
struct_fields.evidence: As for +0x105C. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: as for +0x105C.

struct_fields.name: num_of_allies
struct_fields.comment: A plain count. **Likely** the `num_of_allies` keyword's field, read by `CNumOfAlliesTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D8FD0). Note that it is *not* the list at +0xF88 that `findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md` found the `ally` scope walking and declined to name.
struct_fields.evidence: As for +0x105C, plus the negative: the body reads one dword and no list, so it cannot be a count of +0xF88 computed on the spot. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: as for +0x105C.

struct_fields.name: num_of_vassals
struct_fields.comment: A plain count. **Likely** the `num_of_vassals` keyword's field, read by `CNumOfVassalsTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D9550).
struct_fields.evidence: As for +0x105C. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: as for +0x105C.

struct_fields.name: total_sea_battles
struct_fields.comment: A plain count - the operand is divided by 1000 before the comparison, so the field is a whole number. **Likely** the `total_sea_battles` keyword's field, read by `CTotalSeaBattlesTrigger::Evaluate` (0x600060). The four fields +0x1070..+0x107C are read by four consecutive `CValueTrigger` leaves and sit immediately below the three `*_battles_fought` counters at +0x1080..+0x1088 that the savegame already names, so they are one war-statistics block.
struct_fields.evidence: The body was read end to end: the divide-by-1000 magic operates on `ecx`, loaded from `[ecx+0x40]`, so it is the operand that is scaled and the field that is whole. The name is the class's keyword and the position in the run; the savegame writes no key for it. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a writer elsewhere storing thousandths here, which would make `total_sea_battles = 5` ask for 5000 battles. That is the specific thing this entry is `inferred` about.

struct_fields.name: total_offensives
struct_fields.comment: A plain count, the operand divided by 1000 before comparison. **Likely** the `total_offensives` keyword's field, read by `CTotalOffensivesTrigger::Evaluate` (0x600610). BlackICE's two uses are `total_offensives = 5` and `= 10`, which read as counts.
struct_fields.evidence: As for +0x1070. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: as for +0x1070.

struct_fields.name: total_defensives
struct_fields.comment: A plain count, the operand divided by 1000 before comparison. **Likely** the `total_defensives` keyword's field, read by `CTotalDefensivesTrigger::Evaluate` (0x601170).
struct_fields.evidence: As for +0x1070. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: as for +0x1070.

struct_fields.name: total_we_bomb
struct_fields.comment: A plain number, the operand divided by 1000 before comparison. **Likely** the `total_we_bomb` keyword's field, read by `CTotalWeBombTrigger::Evaluate` (0x600BC0).
struct_fields.evidence: As for +0x1070. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: as for +0x1070.

struct_fields.name: national_unity
struct_fields.comment: **National unity, in thousandths** - the field `national_unity = N` reads, and the input `CCountry::GetSurrenderProgress` divides by 100 to get its 0..1000 answer.
struct_fields.evidence: Two independent sources. The savegame writes `national_unity=81.752` in a country block, three decimals. And `CCountry::GetSurrenderProgress` (0xFCB80) reads +0x10B8, multiplies by 1000 and divides by 100000, then clamps the result to 0..1000 - arithmetic that only makes sense if +0x10B8 runs to 100000, i.e. thousandths of a 0..100 quantity. `CNationalUnityTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F33A0) is the third reader. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a save with `national_unity` above 100.000.

struct_fields.name: organisation_by_ideology
struct_fields.comment: An array of thousandths, one per ideology, indexed by the ideology's own index at `+0x4C`. **Likely** the party-organisation array: `CRulingOrganisationTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F97B0) answers the `organisation` keyword out of `this[ ruling_ideology->+0x4C ]`, and its twin 0x5F9EF0 does the same over +0x10FC for `popularity`.
struct_fields.evidence: Both bodies decoded from their entries; the only difference between them is the displacement, which is what identifies the pair as two arrays over the same index. The names are the two keywords'. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the two arrays being the other way round - nothing here distinguishes them except which keyword reads which, so if `findings/FINDINGS-script.md`'s keyword-to-class table were wrong about `organisation`/`popularity` this pair would swap.

struct_fields.name: popularity_by_ideology
struct_fields.comment: An array of thousandths, one per ideology, indexed by the ideology's own index at `+0x4C`. **Likely** the party-popularity array - the `popularity` keyword reads it through `CRulingPopularityTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F9EF0). See +0x10C4.
struct_fields.evidence: As for +0x10C4. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: as for +0x10C4.

struct_fields.name: ruling_ideology
struct_fields.comment: **The ruling party, and it can be null.** Both `CRulingOrganisationTrigger::Evaluate` and `CRulingPopularityTrigger::Evaluate` load it, return false when it is 0, and then use its `+0x4C` as the index into the two per-ideology arrays at +0x10C4 and +0x10FC. `CIsIdeologyEqualTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F4E80) and `CIdeologyGroupTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F4780) read the same field, which is the second witness - they are the `ideology` and `ideology_group` keywords. The pointee class was not identified, hence `void*`.
struct_fields.evidence: Four readers, two decoded end to end (0x5F97B0, 0x5F9EF0) and two identified by displacement set from the family scan (0x5F4E80 reads +0x1140 and +0x5C, 0x5F4780 reads +0x1140 and +0x50). That the `ideology` keyword and the `ruling party organisation` keyword read the same pointer is what makes 'ruling ideology' the reading. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: `+0x4C` on the pointee not being an ideology index, which would leave the two arrays unindexed.

struct_fields.name: lost_ic
struct_fields.comment: Thousandths - **unlike `total_ic`, which is whole IC**. The `lost_IC` keyword's field, read by `CLostICTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F86D0), which is the canonical direct-compare `CValueTrigger` body with no divide in it. **Likely** in name; the scale is read off the body.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x5F86D0 decoded from the entry: seventeen instructions, no divide-by-1000 magic, so the operand arrives in thousandths and is compared as-is. The name is the keyword's. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the field being whole IC, which would make every `lost_IC = n` condition demand a thousand times too much - the asymmetry with `total_ic` four fields away is real and worth a live check.
